evidence.claim: The President has broad executive authority and the armed forces operate under the President's supreme authority, which defines Bolsonaro's 2022 decision space.
evidence.title: Constituição da República Federativa do Brasil
evidence.excerpt: The President has broad executive authority and the armed forces operate under the President's supreme authority, which defines Bolsonaro's 2022 decision space.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Authoritative constitutional text; directly states presidential powers and military command relation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Bolsonaro held this office throughout 2022; the source is institutional rather than personal.
contrary_evidence: Legal authority does not show how Bolsonaro used it in nuclear or existential-risk matters.

evidence.claim: The 2022 constitutional amendment recognized a fuel-price emergency and expanded Auxílio Brasil, Auxílio Gás, trucker aid, and public-transport support through 31 December 2022.
evidence.title: Emenda Constitucional nº 123, de 14 de julho de 2022
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 constitutional amendment recognized a fuel-price emergency and expanded Auxílio Brasil, Auxílio Gás, trucker aid, and public-transport support through 31 December 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary constitutional text promulgated in 2022; direct legal record of federal welfare expansion.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 target year; the emergency and transfer measures were operative in Bolsonaro's final months.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Bolsonaro's federal administration, but Congress promulgated the amendment and the trigger was an external price shock, so attribution is partial rather than purely personal.
contrary_evidence: The measure was emergency relief, not durable social reform.
Implementation and targeting still depended on bureaucracy and municipalities.

evidence.claim: In January 2022, Auxílio Brasil reached 17.5 million families and the waiting list was zeroed, with total spending above R$7.1 billion.
evidence.title: Programa Auxílio Brasil alcança patamar histórico no país
evidence.excerpt: In January 2022, Auxílio Brasil reached 17.5 million families and the waiting list was zeroed, with total spending above R$7.1 billion.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry release with concrete program coverage and expenditure figures for 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Bolsonaro federal administration, though take-up and local delivery were shared with the CadÚnico/SUAS machinery.
contrary_evidence: Coverage alone does not prove adequacy, fairness, or durability.
The release does not show who was newly poor or whether targeting was clean.

evidence.claim: By November 2022 Auxílio Brasil served 21.53 million families, with an investment of R$13 billion and an average payment of R$607.57 per family.
evidence.title: Auxílio Brasil chega a 21,53 milhões de famílias em novembro de 2022
evidence.excerpt: By November 2022 Auxílio Brasil served 21.53 million families, with an investment of R$13 billion and an average payment of R$607.57 per family.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry release with a concrete 2022 coverage and payment snapshot.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Bolsonaro federal administration, but still mediated by registry rules and local administration.
contrary_evidence: A larger transfer program does not by itself show improved living standards or clean targeting.
The election-year timing creates a plausible political-incentive concern.

evidence.claim: The decree defines CadÚnico as the federal instrument for identifying and characterizing low-income families and for accessing and integrating social programs.
evidence.title: D11016
evidence.excerpt: The decree defines CadÚnico as the federal instrument for identifying and characterizing low-income families and for accessing and integrating social programs.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary legal text issued by the Bolsonaro presidency, specifying program architecture and intended social-function use.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Bolsonaro administration action: he promulgated the decree and it shaped the social-program machinery under his government.
contrary_evidence: The decree shows targeting infrastructure, not actual delivery quality.
Better registry design does not guarantee fewer exclusions or fewer wrongful inclusions.

evidence.claim: The instruction established procedures to identify pregnant beneficiaries eligible for the Auxílio Brasil gestante benefit.
evidence.title: INSTRUÇÃO NORMATIVA CONJUNTA Nº 1, DE 4 DE MARÇO DE 2022
evidence.publisher: Ministério do Desenvolvimento e Assistência Social, Família e Combate à Fome
evidence.excerpt: The instruction established procedures to identify pregnant beneficiaries eligible for the Auxílio Brasil gestante benefit.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official rule text describing a targeted benefit for a vulnerable group in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct federal-program design under Bolsonaro, though operational identification depended on local health and social-assistance networks.
contrary_evidence: This is a targeting rule, not a demonstrated outcome.
No delivery or child-welfare impact is shown in the instruction itself.

evidence.claim: The ministry launched Cuida Mais Brasil and said the first-year allocation would be R$194 million to add pediatricians and gynecologic-obstetric doctors to primary care teams.
evidence.title: Ministério da Saúde lança Cuida Mais Brasil para fortalecer atendimento materno-infantil no SUS
evidence.excerpt: The ministry launched Cuida Mais Brasil and said the first-year allocation would be R$194 million to add pediatricians and gynecologic-obstetric doctors to primary care teams.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official health-ministry release with explicit funding and staffing targets for a 2022 program.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Bolsonaro administration action through the federal health ministry, but implementation still depended on local SUS capacity.
contrary_evidence: Announced staffing does not prove full nationwide coverage or sustained quality.
The program's effect on outcomes is not demonstrated in the launch notice.

evidence.claim: Of 38 million children under 13 in Brazil in 2022, 82.9% were attended by any primary-healthcare service, but the general score for child primary healthcare was 5.7, below the minimum quality level of 6.6.
evidence.title: IBGE surveys how parents and responsible persons address child Primary Healthcare for the first time ever
evidence.excerpt: Of 38 million children under 13 in Brazil in 2022, 82.9% were attended by any primary-healthcare service, but the general score for child primary healthcare was 5.7, below the minimum quality level of 6.6.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: National statistical agency survey with explicit access and quality measures for 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is national-system performance under Bolsonaro's administration, but the result is only partially attributable to the president because SUS delivery is shared with states and municipalities.
contrary_evidence: This is an access-and-quality snapshot, not direct proof of presidential competence.
Some service variation is subnational rather than federal.

evidence.claim: By 14 October 2022, polio vaccination coverage for children under 1 was 44.8%, and the national polio campaign had reached 65% of the target public.
evidence.title: No Dia Nacional da Vacinação, Ministério da Saúde reforça importância de manter o Brasil livre de doenças já eliminadas
evidence.excerpt: By 14 October 2022, polio vaccination coverage for children under 1 was 44.8%, and the national polio campaign had reached 65% of the target public.
evidence.source_locator: second and third paragraphs after the lede
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official health-ministry reporting with an explicit 2022 coverage figure and campaign uptake.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Federal campaign coordination is attributable to the Bolsonaro administration, but the low coverage also reflects state/municipal delivery and vaccine hesitancy.
contrary_evidence: Coverage is a shared-system outcome, so the president is not the only actor.
Campaign reach does not by itself show equitable or sustained coverage improvement.

evidence.claim: By December 2022 the ministry said more than 568 million COVID-19 doses had been distributed and that R$38 billion had been invested in vaccination logistics and procurement.
evidence.title: Governo Federal investiu R$ 38 bilhões em vacinas Covid-19 e criou logística inédita, permitindo alta cobertura vacinal dos brasileiros
evidence.excerpt: By December 2022 the ministry said more than 568 million COVID-19 doses had been distributed and that R$38 billion had been invested in vaccination logistics and procurement.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry record of federal crisis-response logistics and spending in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Bolsonaro federal government, although vaccine delivery itself was shared with states and municipalities.
contrary_evidence: Large-scale distribution does not prove efficient management of all health services.
The release is self-evaluative and should be balanced against independent indicators of routine vaccine coverage.

evidence.claim: In April 2022 CadÚnico recorded more than 3.76 million families in traditional and specific groups, including Indigenous and quilombola households, and said these groups required differentiated registration to be prioritized by municipalities.
evidence.title: Cadastro Único ultrapassa a marca de 3,76 milhões de famílias identificadas como Grupos Populacionais Tradicionais e Específicos
evidence.excerpt: In April 2022 CadÚnico recorded more than 3.76 million families in traditional and specific groups, including Indigenous and quilombola households, and said these groups required differentiated registration to be prioritized by municipalities.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and 'Mobilização e crescimento' section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry release with explicit vulnerable-group counts and targeting language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This reflects Bolsonaro-era federal registration and outreach policy, though actual service access still depended heavily on local governments.
contrary_evidence: The page demonstrates registry prioritization more than real-world service improvements.
It does not show whether those groups actually received adequate benefits or services.

evidence.claim: IBGE reported that from 2022 to 2023 poverty fell from 31.6% to 27.4% and extreme poverty fell from 5.9% to 4.4%, establishing the 2022 end-of-term baseline as still very high.
evidence.title: In 2023, poverty in the country drops to lowest level since 2012
evidence.excerpt: IBGE reported that from 2022 to 2023 poverty fell from 31.6% to 27.4% and extreme poverty fell from 5.9% to 4.4%, establishing the 2022 end-of-term baseline as still very high.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: National statistics agency release with explicit 2022 baseline figures.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective on 2022-2023; suitable for end-of-period baseline, not direct 2022 policy attribution.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Contextual only: this is an outcome measure shaped by pandemic aftermath, labor markets, and later policy as well as Bolsonaro-era conditions.
contrary_evidence: The release does not isolate Bolsonaro's contribution to the 2022 baseline.
It is retrospective and partly reflects dynamics after he left office.

evidence.claim: UNICEF reported that 32 million Brazilian children and adolescents lived in multidimensional poverty, with deprivations in income, education, work, housing, water, sanitation, and information.
evidence.title: Há 32 milhões de crianças e adolescentes na pobreza no Brasil, alerta UNICEF
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF reported that 32 million Brazilian children and adolescents lived in multidimensional poverty, with deprivations in income, education, work, housing, water, sanitation, and information.
evidence.source_locator: opening summary and paragraph beginning 'No Brasil, ao menos 32 milhões...'
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF is a highly credible international agency, and the release uses official Brazilian survey series through 2022/2021 data.
evidence.period_fit: Mostly retrospective but anchored in Brazilian survey data through 2022; good for end-of-period social-condition context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly contextual: the report reflects structural deprivation and pandemic-era deterioration, with only partial attribution to Bolsonaro's federal policy choices.
contrary_evidence: The report spans multiple years and is not a direct measure of one ruler-year.
Structural poverty in a large federative state cannot be assigned to the president alone.

evidence.claim: UNICEF and Ipec reported that 2 million children and adolescents aged 11-19 were not attending school in Brazil in 2022, about 11% of the sample.
evidence.title: Dois milhões de crianças e adolescentes de 11 a 19 anos não estão frequentando a escola no Brasil, alerta UNICEF
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF and Ipec reported that 2 million children and adolescents aged 11-19 were not attending school in Brazil in 2022, about 11% of the sample.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF release based on a specific 2022 survey sample, with clear quantitative findings.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Contextual and only partially attributable to Bolsonaro, because schooling depends heavily on subnational governments and post-pandemic effects.
contrary_evidence: The survey measures exclusion, not federal policy causation.
Subnational education management limits direct presidential attribution.

evidence.claim: Using the 2022 census, UNICEF said 2.1 million Brazilian children and adolescents lacked adequate access to drinking water, with disproportionate impacts on Black, Indigenous, North, and Northeast populations.
evidence.title: 2,1 milhões de crianças e adolescentes vivem sem acesso adequado a água no Brasil, alerta UNICEF
evidence.excerpt: Using the 2022 census, UNICEF said 2.1 million Brazilian children and adolescents lacked adequate access to drinking water, with disproportionate impacts on Black, Indigenous, North, and Northeast populations.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and quoted statement from Rodrigo Resende
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Credible UN-agency analysis based on the 2022 census, but published later and therefore retrospective.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective 2024 publication using 2022 census data; strong fit for end-of-period conditions, weaker for direct contemporaneous attribution.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly contextual: water and sanitation are heavily subnational, though federal funding and priority-setting under Bolsonaro mattered indirectly.
contrary_evidence: The report is based on census conditions, not a direct audit of Bolsonaro's decisions.
Sanitation and water provision are shared across federal, state, and municipal levels.

evidence.claim: The II VIGISAN found that 33.1 million people were in hunger in 2022 and that 58.7% of the population experienced some level of food insecurity, with worse outcomes in rural households and among Black and female-headed households.
evidence.title: 2º Inquérito Nacional sobre Insegurança Alimentar no Contexto da Pandemia da Covid-19 no Brasil
evidence.publisher: Rede Brasileira de Pesquisa em Soberania e SAN
evidence.excerpt: The II VIGISAN found that 33.1 million people were in hunger in 2022 and that 58.7% of the population experienced some level of food insecurity, with worse outcomes in rural households and among Black and female-headed households.
evidence.source_locator: opening summary and the sections on rural households and race/gender
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Large national survey by a respected research network, though not an official government statistic and still partly pandemic-period data.
evidence.period_fit: Directly centered on the 2021-2022 fieldwork window and published in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Contextual and only partially attributable to Bolsonaro because the result reflects pandemic, inflation, labor-market, and policy factors together.
contrary_evidence: The survey covers overlapping pandemic and recovery conditions, so causal attribution to Bolsonaro alone is not justified.
It measures household insecurity, not a direct program audit.

evidence.claim: CGU found that many CadÚnico 'families unipessoais' were likely not truly single-person households and noted that 15% of unipersonal families in August 2023 arose from split households, with the biggest movement occurring in July 2022 when Auxílio Brasil beneficiaries began receiving R$600 regardless of composition.
evidence.title: CGU avalia os procedimentos de inclusão e de averiguação cadastral de famílias unipessoais no CadÚnico
evidence.excerpt: CGU found that many CadÚnico 'families unipessoais' were likely not truly single-person households and noted that 15% of unipersonal families in August 2023 arose from split households, with the biggest movement occurring in July 2022 when Auxílio Brasil beneficiaries began receiving R$600 regardless of composition.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official anti-corruption/audit body reporting with concrete control-failure findings tied to the 2022 benefit structure.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective audit of 2022 program conditions; strong for control and targeting assessment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Bolsonaro-era CadÚnico/Auxílio Brasil controls, though the audit is retrospective and does not by itself prove intentional vote-buying.
contrary_evidence: This shows weak controls and possible opportunism, but not definitive proof of intentional personalist welfare manipulation.
Some problematic records may reflect administrative capacity failures rather than deliberate abuse.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 Bolsonaro-specific nuclear command, crisis, or near-use choice is evidenced.
Direct forensic proof of hidden self-dealing or office-linked family enrichment remains thin.
Broader durable non-electoral program execution is thinner than the campaign-and-power-retention record.

run_provenance.source_mix_note: Rich source metadata and chapter-specific reviewer exclusions were preserved during deterministic conversion.
